title: Firms the City barred, in other public bodies’ records
question: Does a firm the City suspended or barred from its own contracts hold work with the school district, City College, BART or another public body?
finding: 2 firms on the City’s suspended-and-debarred list appear in 9 board items of other bodies worth $96.1 million as read; 2 items ($4.3 million) are dated after the City acted. The largest is ProVen Management, Inc.: 8 BART items, $75.6 million, of which 2 ($4.3 million) are change orders and settlements dated after the City suspended it.
how: Each firm on the City’s current suspended-and-debarred page and in the Controller’s semi-annual reports is searched for, by full name, in the item text of the other bodies. State labor debarments and California entries on the federal exclusion list were searched the same way in the other bodies’ papers and matched nothing there. (That says nothing about the City’s own payees: the screens under “Contractors across agencies, bids and enforcement lists” test those.)
limits: These are board agenda items and resolutions: a ceiling the board was asked to authorise, not a payment, and the dollar figure is the first one a parser found in the text. An item on an agenda may have been amended or withdrawn. Each body is legally separate from the City. A City suspension binds only the City; another body may keep, amend or settle a contract signed earlier, and the later items here are change orders and settlements on contracts awarded before the City acted. Names are matched as text.
